concepts.name: Ecosystem and its components
concepts.description: An ecosystem is all the interacting organisms of an area (biotic components) together with its non-living physical factors (abiotic components); forests, ponds and lakes are natural, gardens, crop-fields and aquaria human-made.

concepts.name: Producers
concepts.description: Green plants and certain bacteria make organic compounds from inorganic substances by photosynthesis, fixing the Sun's energy for the rest of the ecosystem.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1, p.209 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Consumers
concepts.description: Organisms that consume food made by producers, directly or by feeding on other consumers; classed as herbivores, carnivores, omnivores and parasites.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1, p.209 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Decomposers
concepts.description: Microorganisms (bacteria and fungi) break down dead remains and wastes from complex organic into simple inorganic substances that return to the soil for plants.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1, p.209 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Food chains and trophic levels
concepts.description: Each step of a food chain is a trophic level: producers first, herbivores (primary consumers) second, small carnivores (secondary) third, large carnivores (tertiary) fourth; lower levels have more individuals.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1.1, p.210 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Energy flow and the 10 percent law
concepts.description: Plants capture about 1% of sunlight as food energy; about 10% of the food at one level reaches the next, so energy flow is unidirectional, diminishes at each level and limits chains to three or four steps.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1.1, p.210-211 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Food webs
concepts.description: Because each organism is usually eaten by two or more kinds of organisms, feeding relationships form branching lines, a food web of many interconnected food chains.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1.1, p.210-211 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Biological magnification
concepts.description: Non-degradable chemicals such as pesticides enter food chains from soil and water and accumulate progressively at each trophic level, reaching the highest concentration in humans at the top.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.1.1, p.211-212 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Ozone layer and its depletion
concepts.description: Ozone (O3), formed when UV radiation splits O2, shields the Earth from the Sun's UV radiation in the upper atmosphere; CFCs have depleted it, and a 1987 UNEP agreement froze CFC production.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.2.1, p.212-213 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)

concepts.name: Biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances
concepts.description: Substances broken down by biological processes are biodegradable; others, such as many plastics that enzymes cannot act on, are non-biodegradable and persist or harm the ecosystem; managing the garbage we produce.
concepts.evidence: NCERT Class 10 Science §13.2.2, p.213-215 (excerpt kept in evidence.local.json)
